name: Street Redesign Choice: Greenery, Bike Lanes and Social Space
description: Faithful replication of the static-image condition of Wicki, Sinatra, Huang & Kaufmann (2026), "Space for people, not cars: a large-scale visual choice experiment on urban street redesigns", npj Urban Sustainability (Swiss Mobility Panel wave 6, N = 5,991). Participants answer whether they can ride a bicycle, their support for the E-Bike City proposal (1–7), satisfaction with street design (1–7), the three most important aspects of street remodelling, and three pairwise importance ratings (road infrastructure, environmental protection, quality of life). Each participant is randomly assigned a main road or a side street in Zurich, rates the current street (would like to live there; would cycle there), then sees two different redesigns drawn at random from 12 combinations of infrastructure (low / medium / high), greenery (low / high) and social space (low / high). For each redesign they write what they think of it and rate support in a popular vote, willingness to live there and willingness to cycle there (1–7). Finally they see both redesigns side by side with infrastructure cost per km (scenario base cost × 0.8, 1 or 1.2, using the cost values in the authors' data), financing (city / federal / 50-50) and average cycling time (3–6 min), and choose between them for voting, living and cycling. Cycling questions are only shown to people who can ride a bicycle. Question wording follows the authors' English survey instrument; condition codes (MainPic / NeigPic, iHigh-eLow-sHigh etc.) match the authors' replication data. Images: the authors' street visualisations (Photoshop composites from photographs of Zurich streets) and instrument from OSF 9g4fj, used with credit to the authors; the template will be removed if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) only the static-image groups are included; the original also randomised half of the respondents to navigable 360° views; (2) the wording of the financing lines in the choice table is ours (the instrument shows them only as placeholders); (3) the panel's other survey blocks and the sociodemographic questions taken from earlier waves are left out; (4) the consent text is shortened and does not name the Swiss Mobility Panel.
author: Wicki, Sinatra, Huang & Kaufmann

config.description: Space for people, not cars: a visual choice experiment on urban street redesigns. Each participant is randomly assigned a main road or a side street in Zurich. After rating the current street, they see two redesigns that vary in cycling and pedestrian infrastructure (low / medium / high), greenery (low / high) and social space (low / high), rate each, and then choose between them with costs, financing and cycling time shown. Rebuilt from Wicki, Sinatra, Huang and Kaufmann (2026), npj Urban Sustainability, with the authors' visualisations and survey instrument from OSF 9g4fj.
